title: Resilient Fallback Sampler and Ephemeral Quarantine Controller
author: Aisha Patel
description: Motivation: During recent regional spikes we observed cascading circuit flips caused by aggressive global fallback heuristics and a lack of short-lived isolation for noisy tenants. This PR introduces two complementary runtime components: 1) a fallback sampler that probabilistically exercises lower-cost fallback paths to maintain observability of fallback quality and avoid cold surprises, and 2) an ephemeral quarantine controller that isolates tenants showing short-lived pathological behavior into a soft-eviction lane for a bounded window. Design summary: - Fallback sampler: routes a controlled fraction of traffic (configurable per-tenant, default 1%) to candidate fallback models/regions to gather quality metrics without impacting live traffic. Sampling policy is weight-decayed and tied to per-tenant SLO delta signals so we increase sampling when drift is suspected. - Ephemeral quarantine controller: detects rapid SLO deterioration patterns (burst error-rate, latency amplification, KV-thrashing) and moves matching traffic into a low-priority quarantine bucket for N seconds (configurable TTL). Quarantine is non-blocking: requests are still served with lower resource priority and the controller stages a gradual readmit with a short warmup. Key goals: reduce global circuit oscillations, limit blast radius of noisy tenants, and get early feedback on fallback model regressions. Checklist: [x] design doc linked (Linear ENG-2489) [x] unit + integration tests for sampler toggles and quota accounting [x] runtime metrics + dashboards added [x] safe defaults and feature flags for rollout [x] short-lived hotfix path to disable quarantine if needed Rolling strategy: feature gated behind runtime flag fallback_sampler.enabled and quarantine.enabled. Default rollout: 0.5% global, 1% on suspect tenants; quarantine TTL default 60s with exponential cool-off on repeated isolates. Includes runtime knobs for teams to tune per-customer. Backwards compatibility: no protocol changes; all behavior controlled server-side. Hotfix plan: single-command disable via console toggle and emergency cluster-level env var REDWOOD_QUARANTINE=off. Related work: follows ideas from ENG-2410 (graceful-degradation-experiments) and complements the selective-shedder work. Why different from previous PRs: rather than hard failover or broad load-shedding, this PR emphasizes short, observable isolation plus active sampling to reduce surprise regressions when fallback models are used.

change_summary: Adds sampled fallback routing and a short-lived tenant quarantine lane to reduce SLO oscillation and provide low-risk fallback quality telemetry. Includes config, tests, dashboards, and emergency disable path.
review_comments: Marco Jensen: Strong idea. Please add a metric for 'quarantine.injected_rate' and group by tenant tier. Also add an alert for repeated quarantines in a 5m window.
Aisha Patel (author): Added quarantine.injected_rate and new alert rule. Grouping by tier is implemented with the 'tier' label on the metric. PTAL.

release_notes: Introduce a fallback sampling mechanism (default 1%) and an ephemeral tenant quarantine controller to reduce cascading circuit flips. Feature is off by default; enable via runtime feature flags. Improvements: reduced oscillation, better fallback telemetry. Hotfix: single-command disable available.
observability_changes: Added fallback_sampler.* metrics (sampled_requests_total, sampled_fallback_success, sampled_fallback_latency) and quarantine.* metrics (quarantine_injected_total, quarantine_active_gauge, quarantine_readmit_events). Dashboard panels for per-tenant sample rates and quarantine churn added.
rollback_instructions: 1) Toggle runtime flags: set fallback_sampler.enabled=false and quarantine.enabled=false via console; 2) If console unavailable, set env REDWOOD_QUARANTINE=off and restart controller pod; 3) Monitor 'quarantine_active_gauge' and 'sampled_requests_total' until zero; 4) If KV-prefetch caused issues, revert commit 5 in the PR and redeploy.
notes_for_release_manager: Coordinate with product teams owning high-volume tenants before enabling beyond 1% sampling. Notify SRE slack #sre-runtime and Pinboard channels. Schedule a 1-hour observation window after ramping to 5%.
post_merge_tasks: 1) Create a small canary pipeline to ramp sampling from 0.5% -> 1% over 2 hours; 2) Add a Linear task to capture early fallback quality regressions (ENG-2521); 3) Run a cross-team readout with product owners.
hotfix_indicator: hotfix path included (scripts/rollout/disable_quarantine.sh). The quarantine piece was toggled on briefly in preview and toggled off for one tenant during validation.
qa_notes: Tested locally with integration harness: simulated bursty latency and error modes, verified quarantine TTL semantics, readmit warmup, and sampled fallback telemetry. Add-on test: end-to-end smoke with example fallback_sampler_demo.yaml.
security_notes: Sampler respects tenant opt-out and does not send request bodies to external metrics endpoints. All telemetry emitted adheres to PII filtering rules. Quarantine controller runs inside control-plane namespace with limited RBAC.
follow_up: Track fallback quality regressions in ENG-2521; consider adaptive sampling (closed-loop) if false-positive rate grows. Evaluate longer quarantine strategies for repeat offenders.
